proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a finite revealed simple regular graph \(G\).  A single proposal draws a uniform \(k\)-subset \(A\), computes \(F_G(A)\) by exploring graph distance at most two from each vertex of \(A\), and tests whether \(|F_G(A)|\ge k\).  Each depth-two exploration examines at most \(1+d+d(d-1)\) incidences.  Thus one proposal uses a number of elementary operations polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\).  There are at most \(n^3\) proposals.  If one is accepted, a uniform \(k\)-subset \(C\subseteq F_G(A)\), the coin \(\omega\), and at most \(n\) remaining fair assignment coins are drawn; if none is accepted, only the fair global coin is drawn.  These are all finite uniform draws from explicitly listed finite sets.  Therefore \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) can be sampled exactly in randomized time polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\), by \(\text{def:reservoir-capsule}\).

For the finite audit, let \(\Omega_G\) be the latent sample space whose atoms record the ordered list of no more than \(n^3\) reservoir proposals, the first accepted proposal and the subsequent \(C\) when acceptance occurs, \(\omega\), and all assignment coins used by the construction.  The set \(\Omega_G\) is finite.  For each \(\eta\in\Omega_G\), the construction gives an explicit rational mass \(p_G(\eta)\), and the maps
\[
 \eta\longmapsto Z^{\mathrm{cap}}(\eta),
 \qquad
 \eta\longmapsto X_u(\eta)
\]
are deterministic.  Hence, for every \(u\), finite summation gives
\[
 \pi_u=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G}p_G(\eta)X_u(\eta). \tag{1}
\]
Every summand in (1) is a nonnegative rational number, so exact rational arithmetic both computes \(\pi_u\) and decides whether it is zero.  Repeating (1) for the \(2n\) exposure vertices therefore detects whether \(\min_u\pi_u>0\).

Assume for the remainder of the evaluation argument that \(\pi_u>0\) for all \(u\).  For \(u,v\in\mathcal U\), the same enumeration computes
\[
 q_{uv}:=\Pr(X_u=X_v=1\mid G)
 =\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G}p_G(\eta)X_u(\eta)X_v(\eta). \tag{2}
\]
The denominators in \(q_{uv}/(\pi_u\pi_v)\) are now nonzero.  Substitution of (1)--(2) into \(\text{def:normalized-kernel}\) computes every entry of \(\Gamma_G\) exactly.

For an accepted atom, \(\text{prop:capsule-realization}\) says that every endpoint outcome multiplied by a nonzero focal indicator in \(\widetilde\tau_G\) is revealed by \((Z^{\mathrm{cap}},y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}))\).  On a fallback atom every focal indicator is zero.  Thus \(\text{def:raw-estimator}\), together with the already computed positive inclusion probabilities, evaluates \(\widetilde\tau_G(\eta)\) exactly on every latent atom using only the atom's focal metadata and the outcomes observed under its assignment.

Fix an assignment \(z\) having positive probability and define its finite fiber
\[
 \Omega_G(z)=\{\eta\in\Omega_G:Z^{\mathrm{cap}}(\eta)=z\}.
\]
Because the potential-outcome schedule is fixed, \(y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}})\) is a deterministic function of \(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}\).  Consequently conditioning on \((G,Z^{\mathrm{cap}},y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}))=(G,z,y(z))\) selects the same latent fiber as conditioning on \((G,Z^{\mathrm{cap}})=(G,z)\).  Its denominator
\[
 P_G(z):=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G(z)}p_G(\eta)
\]
is positive.  The conditional expectation in \(\text{def:observed-estimator}\) is therefore the explicit finite ratio
\[
 \widehat\tau_G(G,z,y(z))
 =\frac{\displaystyle
       \sum_{\eta\in\Omega_G(z)}p_G(\eta)\widetilde\tau_G(\eta)}
      {\displaystyle P_G(z)}. \tag{3}
\]
Equation (3) computes both the conditional weights \(p_G(\eta)/P_G(z)\) and the value of \(\widehat\tau_G\).  The realization proposition ensures that every outcome needed in its numerator is a coordinate of \(y(z)\); internal focal metadata are summed out.  Since there are finitely many positive-probability observed-data atoms, (3) also proves measurability.  This enumeration claim is exact but is not a polynomial-time claim.

The positivity qualification is necessary even in the smallest admissible population.  Take \(n=4\), \(d=3\), and \(G=K_4\).  Then \(k=1\), while every vertex is within distance two of every singleton \(A\), so \(F_G(A)=\varnothing\).  All \(n^3\) proposals fail, the fallback is used, and \(X_u=0\) for every \(u\).  Therefore \(\pi_u=0\) for every \(u\), which (1) detects, whereas the divisions defining \(\Gamma_G\), \(\widetilde\tau_G\), and \(\widehat\tau_G\) under their displayed positive-inclusion formulas are unavailable.  Thus the design law is total for every finite \(G\), but exact kernel and estimator evaluation has precisely the stated positive-inclusion domain.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every finite revealed graph \(G\), an exact draw from \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) can be generated in randomized time polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\). Finite enumeration of the capped latent sample space computes every \(\pi_u\) and detects whether any \(\pi_u\) is zero. If every \(\pi_u>0\), the same enumeration computes every entry of \(\Gamma_G\), evaluates \(\widetilde\tau_G\) on every latent atom, and computes every conditional weight and value defining \(\widehat\tau_G\) on each positive-probability observed-data atom. Under this positivity condition, \(\widehat\tau_G\) is a finite measurable observed-data function and is exactly auditable without observing internal focal metadata. Exact enumeration is not asserted to run in polynomial time.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unconditional estimator-totality claim is false. For the admissible smallest instance \(n=4\), \(d=3\), and \(G=K_4\), one has \(k=1\) and \(F_G(A)=\varnothing\) for every singleton \(A\); the fallback is certain and every \(\pi_u=0\). Enumeration always detects this case, but the normalized kernel and the positive-inclusion estimator formulas may be evaluated only after positivity is verified.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Can the local handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be developed into an algorithm running in time polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\) that evaluates or approximates \(\widehat\tau_G\) from \((G,Z^{\mathrm{cap}},y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}))\), and returns an observable certificate \(U_G\) satisfying \[\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]\le U_G?\] Can such a certificate either establish \(U_G=O(r(n,d))\) on a probability-\(1-o(1)\) random-regular graph event, or furnish a rigorous obstruction to \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(n/k)\), while numerical approximation error contributes \(o(r(n,d))\)? If a balanced-hole lower edge at scale \(r(n,d)\) is separately established, an affirmative compiler and \(O(n/k)\) certificate could potentially close the resulting logarithmic bracket for \(R_2(G)\) and make the capsule deployable; it would not implement an already established matched minimax theorem. Both the polynomial-time algorithmic construction and the capsule spectral bound remain open, and the proved upper bound uses a different published Conflict Graph Design.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unqualified supremum ranges beyond the frozen endpoint-\(L^2\) ANI class and is not the paper's risk claim. The consumer also overstated what a compiler would implement: the capsule norm bound and the strengthened random-regular lower edge require separate proofs.

proposed.comparator_claim: For random \(d\)-regular \(G\) with \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), the published growing-degree bracket is \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) with probability \(1-o(1)\).

Lemma 3.3 gives closed-form desired-exposure probabilities, Lemma 4.2 gives local covariance bounds, and Theorem 4.1 bounds modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by \(12.5\lambda(H_G)/n\) times the two endpoint empirical second moments after the GATE spectral identification.
The neighborhood-union construction gives a one-sided treated-component upper bound under controlled codegrees and leaves the full estimator open.
A greedy independent focal set has size at least \(n\log s/s\) with high probability in the paper's Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi regime.
Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 compare uniform root mean-squared error of a design-based Riesz estimator with the scaled norm of its variance operator.
The largest balanced independent sets in generic random bipartite graphs have density \((2+o_d(1))\log d/d\), with a factor-two local-algorithm barrier.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The unaudited strengthened random-regular lower edge cannot be positioned as a strict tightening of the published minimax bracket; the comparator table must record only the supported equivalence until the balanced-hole estimate is proved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a polynomial-time observed-data approximation to \(\widehat\tau_G\) and an observable operator-norm risk certificate valid uniformly over \(y\in\mathcal M_2(G)\), with numerical contribution \(o(r(n,d))\); separately prove \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(n/k)\) on the required random-regular event or certify an obstruction.
open_obligations.obstruction: Exact enumeration is finite but exponential. Simulation error bounds depend on an inverse-polynomial lower bound for \(\min_u\pi_u\), while simulation of the Rao--Blackwell ratio also depends on the probability of the realized assignment fiber. Neither lower bound, nor a contraction, mixing-time, approximate-counting, or deterministic spectral certificate, is supplied by the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: I extended the finite-enumeration reduction with simultaneous Chebyshev bounds for all inclusion and joint-inclusion probabilities and an explicit entrywise-to-operator-norm conversion. This gives pointwise approximation when positive overlap is quantitatively known, but does not control the conditional Rao--Blackwell fiber or furnish the required uniform polynomial bound.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For every fixed finite \(G\), finite enumeration computes all inclusion probabilities and detects zero inclusion; when \(p:=\min_u\pi_u>0\), it computes \(\Gamma_G\), \(\widetilde\tau_G\), and \(\widehat\tau_G\) exactly.  There is also a pointwise simulation audit.  Fix an integer \(m\ge1\), draw \(m\) independent copies from \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\), and define \(q_{uv}:=\mathbb E[X_uX_v\mid G]\), \(\widehat\pi_u=m^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^mX_u^{(s)}\), and \(\widehat q_{uv}=m^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^mX_u^{(s)}X_v^{(s)}\).  All probabilities in this paragraph are conditional on the fixed \(G\).  Independence and the fact that a Bernoulli variance is at most \(1/4\) give \(\mathbb E[(\widehat\pi_u-\pi_u)^2\mid G]\le1/(4m)\), and the same bound holds for \(\widehat q_{uv}-q_{uv}\).  On the event \(|W|>\varepsilon\), one has \(W^2>\varepsilon^2\), so \(\varepsilon^2\Pr(|W|>\varepsilon\mid G)\le\mathbb E[W^2\mid G]\).  Applying this elementary inequality and then summing the event probabilities over \(2n\) indices or \(4n^2\) ordered pairs gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\max_u|\widehat\pi_u-\pi_u|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{n}{2m\varepsilon^2},
 \qquad
 \Pr\!\left(\max_{u,v}|\widehat q_{uv}-q_{uv}|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{n^2}{m\varepsilon^2}. \tag{4}
\]
If \(\varepsilon\le p/2\), then every \(\widehat\pi_u\ge p/2\).  On this event define
\[
 \widehat\Gamma_{uv}
 :=s_as_b\left\{\frac{\widehat q_{uv}}
 {\widehat\pi_u\widehat\pi_v}-1\right\},
 \qquad u=(i,a),\quad v=(j,b).
\]
Since \(0\le q_{uv}\le1\), direct subtraction of the two normalized ratios gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat q_{uv}}{\widehat\pi_u\widehat\pi_v}
       -\frac{q_{uv}}{\pi_u\pi_v}\right|
 \le \frac{4\varepsilon}{p^2}
 +\frac{|\pi_u\pi_v-\widehat\pi_u\widehat\pi_v|}
 {\widehat\pi_u\widehat\pi_v\pi_u\pi_v}
 \le \frac{4\varepsilon}{p^2}+\frac{8\varepsilon}{p^4}.
\]
Substitution in the normalized-kernel formula and the bound of an operator norm by the largest absolute row sum now yield
\[
 \max_{u,v}|\widehat\Gamma_{uv}-\Gamma_{uv}|
 \le \frac{4\varepsilon}{p^2}+\frac{8\varepsilon}{p^4}
 \le \frac{12\varepsilon}{p^4},
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Gamma-\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le \frac{24n\varepsilon}{p^4}. \tag{5}
\]
Thus pointwise covariance-action approximation is explicit, but its sample guarantee depends on an a priori lower bound for \(p\), which the unresolved capsule-kernel question does not provide.  Moreover, rejection-based simulation of the conditional ratio defining \(\widehat\tau_G\) depends on the probability of the realized assignment fiber, for which no inverse-polynomial lower bound is available.  Finally, an additive entrywise estimate is not by itself the requested uniform risk certificate: over the endpoint \(L^2\) ball, an \(o(r(n,d))\) risk error requires operator-norm error \(o(nr(n,d))\).  Hence (4)--(5) give a computable fixed-instance audit but not the requested uniform polynomial-time compiler.

prose_updates.tldr: For fixed potential outcomes under arbitrary neighborhood interference on a revealed random \(d\)-regular graph, the fully audited unconditional comparison is the published-order bracket: uniformly for feasible \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), with probability \(1-o(1)\), \(c(d+1)/n\le R_2(G)\le C(1+d^2)/n\). For fixed \(d\), this gives \(R_2(G)=\Theta_d(n^{-1})\). The proposed stronger lower edge \(r(n,d)=(d+1)^2/[n\log(d+2)]\) still requires a valid random-regular balanced-hole theorem. The reservoir capsule has exact covariance identities and an exact finite audit conditional on positive focal inclusion, but its \(O(n/k)\) norm bound, scalable compiler, and logarithmically improved risk remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published unrestricted minimax theory places growing-degree random-regular full-GATE risk between orders \(d/n\) and \(d^2/n\). A deterministic balanced-hole Bayes reduction can identify the graph certificate needed for the stronger lower scale, but the required uniform random-regular switching comparison has not been proved or anchored by a matching primary theorem.
project_justification.niche: The two-copy exposure graph and balanced reservoir capsule expose exact covariance structure and a concrete computational target. They isolate two unresolved tasks: the accepted compatible-pair operator bound and a polynomial-time observed-data compiler with auditable error.
project_justification.fill: The paper retains the supported all-procedure lower comparison and the observed-data adaptation of the published conflict-graph upper design, records the \(\Theta_d(n^{-1})\) fixed-degree benchmark, proves the capsule's exact finite covariance algebra, and supplies a finite evaluator that detects zero inclusion before computing kernel or estimator formulas. It does not claim an exact frontier or capsule attainment.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on the revealed \(G\), the proved upper guarantee uses the outcome-independent published Conflict Graph Design and an observed-data Rao--Blackwellized modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator. The capped balanced reservoir law \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) is a separate candidate whose sharper covariance rate and scalable evaluation are open.
sampling_model.units: The finite population \(V\) and its potential-outcome schedule are fixed conditional on \(G\); assignment is the only inferential randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Both designs generate one binary assignment. The published design resolves requested endpoint exposures by a conflict-graph importance ordering; the capsule forces the closed neighborhoods of its two focal reservoirs to opposite arms and randomizes the remainder.
sampling_model.overlap: The published design's desired-exposure probabilities are explicitly positive under its closed-form construction. The finite capsule evaluator always computes and checks every \(\pi_u\); uniform order-\(k/n\) capsule overlap is unresolved and is never presumed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no super-population nuisances. Published desired-exposure weights have closed forms. When every capsule inclusion probability is positive, capsule inclusions, covariance entries, and Rao--Blackwell weights are exact finite-design functionals computable by enumeration; enumeration may be exponential and polynomial-time uniform approximation remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje define the same endpoint-\(L^2\) unrestricted minimax experiment and prove the growing-degree random-regular bracket \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) under \(d=o(\sqrt n)\). The attempted strengthening of its lower edge to \(r(n,d)\) reduces to a balanced-hole estimate, but the needed simple-random-regular switching counts are not yet verified. Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw provide the closed upper route used here: Lemma 3.3 gives exact desired-exposure probabilities, Lemma 4.2 controls local normalized covariances, and Theorem 4.1 gives the \(O(\lambda(H_G)/n)\) modified Horvitz--Thompson variance bound. Li and Li prove only a treated-component result. Harshaw, S\"avje, and Wang motivate operator-norm risk analysis, while Perkins and Wang and Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi study balanced or independent sets in different graph and estimand settings; none supplies the acceptance-conditioned two-arm capsule covariance estimate or compiler required here.
prose_updates.interpretation: The supported bracket rules out risk below the published lower order and gives the ordinary \(n^{-1}\) benchmark at every fixed degree, but it does not determine the growing-degree frontier. A valid balanced-hole theorem would strengthen the all-procedure lower edge to \(r(n,d)\). Independently, an \(O(n/k)\) capsule norm certificate would yield a sharper observed-data upper construction. Both advances remain separate obligations.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Two nontrivial steps remain unresolved. First, the proposed random-regular balanced-hole estimate needs uniform switching counts that explicitly control simple-graph invalid moves, exceptional internal-edge strata, and the available half-edge event. Second, the capsule's accepted compatible-pair covariance block contains the random denominator \(\binom{|F_G(A)|}{k}\), and neither entrywise bounds nor pointwise Monte Carlo supplies the required operator-norm certificate or efficient conditional Rao--Blackwell weights. No switching, covariance, overlap, or computational premise is added to assume either crux.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper does not prove the strengthened random-regular lower edge, an exact minimax frontier, or capsule attainment at \(d^2/[n\log d]\). It does prove or retain the supported published-order bracket and the fixed-degree \(\Theta_d(n^{-1})\) benchmark. The capsule assignment law is total, but its normalized kernel and estimator audit are asserted only after finite enumeration verifies every \(\pi_u>0\); \(G=K_4\) at \(n=4\) is an explicit zero-inclusion witness. Exact enumeration may be exponential, and scalable certification remains open. No studentized central limit theorem, bounded-outcome model, additive interference model, or real-network random-regular approximation is claimed.

proofs.proof_tex:
The fixed-graph certificate \(\text{lem:balanced-hole-bayes-lower}\) gives, for every revealed graph and without an asymptotic condition,
\[
R_2(G)\ge\frac1{16n}. \tag{16}
\]
This conclusion already ranges over all outcome-independent designs and all measurable, possibly biased or randomized estimators because those are the procedures in \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\), and the proof of the certificate took the infimum over that entire class.

For the growing-degree contribution, Corollary 5.4 of Kandiros, Harshaw, and S\"avje, materialized as \(\text{lem:published-random-regular-gate-lower}\), states that there is a universal \(c_0>0\) and events \(L_n\), measurable with respect to \(G_n\), such that
\[
\Pr_{G_n}(L_n)\longrightarrow1,
\qquad
R_2(G)\ge c_0\frac d n\quad\text{on }L_n. \tag{17}
\]
The notation agrees exactly: the cited paper's arbitrary-neighborhood-interference class at moment parameter \(q=2\) imposes, separately on the two GATE endpoint arms, the two empirical second-moment inequalities in \(\text{def:endpoint-class}\); its GATE is the all-treated minus all-control contrast \(\tau_G\); and its minimax risk takes the infimum over outcome-independent designs and estimators, which is \(R_2(G)\) in \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\).  If an estimator additionally uses an independent random seed \(U\), then
\[
\overline T(G,Z,y(Z))
=\mathbb E[T(G,Z,y(Z),U)\mid G,Z,y(Z)]
\]
is observed-data measurable and, for each fixed schedule \(y\), conditional Jensen gives
\[
\mathbb E[(\overline T-\tau_G(y))^2\mid G]
\le
\mathbb E[(T-\tau_G(y))^2\mid G].
\]
Thus allowing estimator randomization cannot reduce the minimax risk, and no superpopulation randomness or estimator restriction is introduced in passing from the cited corollary to (17).

On \(L_n\), equations (16)--(17) give
\[
R_2(G)\ge
\max\!\left\{\frac1{16n},c_0\frac d n\right\}
\ge \frac12\left\{\frac1{16n}+c_0\frac d n\right\}
\ge c\frac{1+d}{n}, \tag{18}
\]
where \(c=\tfrac12\min\{1/16,c_0\}>0\) is universal.  Taking probabilities in (18) and using \(\Pr_{G_n}(L_n)\to1\) proves the displayed assertion for every feasible sequence satisfying \(\text{ass:subsqrt-degree}\).

The earlier proposed improvement would require the additional random-graph conclusion
\[
b(G)=O_{\Pr}\!\left(\frac{n\log(d+2)}{(d+1)^2}\right). \tag{19}
\]
Indeed, substituting (19) into (15) would produce the scale \(r(n,d)\).  The previously supplied switching sketch did not define the exposure-conditioned residual degree sequences or switching strata and did not establish uniform valid-to-invalid forward and reverse counts after excluding loops, repeated edges, exceptional internal-edge levels, and shortages of available half-edges.  Corollary 5.4 supplies (17), not (19).  Therefore (19) is not used here, and the theorem honestly stops at (18).

By the repaired theorem \(\text{thm:all-procedure-lower}\), there are a universal \(c>0\) and events \(L_n\) such that
\[
\Pr_{G_n}(L_n)\longrightarrow1,
\qquad
R_2(G)\ge c\frac{1+d}{n}\quad\text{on }L_n. \tag{20}
\]

We derive an upper bound that is valid for every revealed simple \(d\)-regular graph, including bounded \(d\).  Fix such a graph and a schedule \(y\in\mathcal M_2(G)\).  The cited finite-sample Conflict Graph Design result \(\text{lem:published-conflict-graph-risk}\) supplies an outcome-independent design and a modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator \(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\), possibly using the design's internal desired-exposure metadata, such that
\[
\mathbb E(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G)=\tau_G(y) \tag{21}
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G)
\le \frac{12.5\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}
\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}y_{i1}^2+
\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}y_{i0}^2\right\}, \tag{22}
\]
where \((B_G)_{ij}=\mathbf1\{\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\}\).

To place this estimator in the observed-data class of \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\), define
\[
T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}
=\mathbb E[T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G,Z,y(Z)]. \tag{23}
\]
All relevant assignment and auxiliary spaces are finite, and the auxiliary law is fixed by the observed graph.  Thus (23) is the same finite conditional sum for every schedule and is a measurable function of \((G,Z,y(Z))\), with any value assigned on assignments of design probability zero.  The tower property and (21) give
\[
\mathbb E(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}\mid G)=\tau_G(y). \tag{24}
\]
The conditional variance identity gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G)
=\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}\mid G)
+\mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(T_{\mathrm{CG}}\mid G,Z,y(Z))\mid G], \tag{25}
\]
so (22), (24), and the nonnegativity of the final term imply
\[
\mathbb E[(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}-\tau_G)^2\mid G]
\le \frac{12.5\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}
\left\{\frac1n\sum_i y_{i1}^2+
\frac1n\sum_i y_{i0}^2\right\}. \tag{26}
\]
By \(\text{def:endpoint-class}\), each average in braces is at most one.  The proved spectral map \(\text{lem:gate-conflict-spectral-map}\) gives \(\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\lambda(H_G)\le1+d^2\).  Hence (26) yields, uniformly over the class,
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}
\mathbb E[(T_{\mathrm{CG}}^{\mathrm{RB}}-\tau_G)^2\mid G]
\le25\frac{1+d^2}{n}. \tag{27}
\]
The design and estimator in (23) are admissible in \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\); evaluating its infimum at this pair proves the deterministic inequality
\[
R_2(G)\le25\frac{1+d^2}{n}. \tag{28}
\]

Intersecting the sure event (28) with \(L_n\), equations (20) and (28) prove the probability statement with \(C=25\).  If \(d\) is fixed, the deterministic lower branch of \(\text{lem:balanced-hole-bayes-lower}\) and (28) give, for every revealed graph,
\[
\frac1{16n}\le R_2(G)\le25\frac{1+d^2}{n}, \tag{29}
\]
which is exactly \(R_2(G)=\Theta_d(n^{-1})\).

For the smallest admissible case \(n=4,d=0\), (29) reads \(1/64\le R_2(G)\le25/4\) when the sharper value \(b(G)=2\) from the finite audit is used on the left; hence no positivity, division, or boundary case is lost at the no-interference elbow.  For growing \(d\), the ratio of the deterministic upper endpoint in (28) to the proved random-regular lower endpoint in (20) is of order at most \(d\), not of logarithmic order.  Obtaining the formerly claimed logarithmic-width bracket would require the unproved balanced-hole estimate (19), so neither that estimate nor capsule attainment is inferred from (20)--(29).

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(n\ge4\) and a revealed simple graph \(G\) on \(V\).  For \(z\in\{0,1\}^V\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
E_a(z)=\{i\in V:z_j=a\text{ for every }j\in N_G[i]\},
\qquad
b(G)=\max_{z\in\{0,1\}^V}\min\{|E_1(z)|,|E_0(z)|\}.
\]
Then the unrestricted design-based minimax risk satisfies the deterministic inequalities
\[
R_2(G)\ge \frac{1}{32\max\{1,b(G)\}}\ge \frac{1}{16n}.
\]
The first inequality holds simultaneously against every outcome-independent assignment law and every measurable, possibly biased or randomized estimator on \(\mathcal M_2(G)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(B=\max\{1,b(G)\}\).  We first record two deterministic consequences of the definitions.  Since \(i\in N_G[i]\), a unit cannot belong to both \(E_1(z)\) and \(E_0(z)\).  Hence, for every assignment \(z\),
\[
\min\{|E_1(z)|,|E_0(z)|\}
\le \frac{|E_1(z)|+|E_0(z)|}{2}
\le \frac n2. \tag{1}
\]
Taking the maximum over \(z\) gives \(b(G)\le n/2\).  Because \(n\ge4\), it follows also that
\[
1\le B\le \frac n2. \tag{2}
\]
Moreover, if \(i\in E_1(z)\) and \(j\in E_0(z)\), then \(N_G[i]\cap N_G[j]=\varnothing\): a vertex in the intersection would be required by the two exposure definitions to have both assignment values.  If \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\), the two closed neighborhoods intersect, at \(i\), at \(j\), or at an intermediate vertex according as the distance is zero, one, or two.  Consequently
\[
i\in E_1(z),\ j\in E_0(z)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)>2. \tag{2a}
\]
Thus \(b(G)\) is indeed the largest balanced two-sided radius-two hole generated by an assignment.

We prove the first inequality by a Bayes reduction whose prior is common to all designs and estimators.  For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), independently draw a Rademacher sign \(B_a\).  Conditional on \(B_a\), independently over \(i\in V\) draw \(\xi_{ia}\in\{-1,1\}\) with
\[
\Pr(\xi_{ia}=1\mid B_a)=\frac{1+\delta B_a}{2},
\qquad
\delta^2=\frac{1}{4B}. \tag{3}
\]
Equation (2) implies \(0<\delta\le1/2\), so the probabilities in (3) are strictly between zero and one.  Define a random fixed potential-outcome schedule by
\[
y_i(z)=
\begin{cases}
\xi_{i1},&z_j=1\text{ for every }j\in N_G[i],\\
\xi_{i0},&z_j=0\text{ for every }j\in N_G[i],\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases} \tag{4}
\]
The first two cases are disjoint because \(N_G[i]\) contains \(i\).  Formula (4) depends on \(z\) only through \(z|_{N_G[i]}\), so it satisfies \(\text{ass:ani}\).  Moreover,
\[
y_{i1}=\xi_{i1},\qquad y_{i0}=\xi_{i0},
\qquad
\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}y_{ia}^2=1\quad(a=0,1). \tag{5}
\]
Thus (5), \(\text{ass:treated-endpoint-l2}\), \(\text{ass:control-endpoint-l2}\), and \(\text{def:endpoint-class}\) show that every realization of the prior belongs to \(\mathcal M_2(G)\), including the boundary of both moment balls.

Fix an arbitrary outcome-independent assignment law and condition on \(Z=z\).  By (4), the observed outcomes reveal precisely \((\xi_{i1}:i\in E_1(z))\), \((\xi_{i0}:i\in E_0(z))\), and deterministic zeros at all remaining units.  Select an arm \(a_*(z)\) attaining the smaller exposure count and put
\[
m=|E_{a_*(z)}(z)|\le b(G)\le B,
\qquad L=n-m. \tag{6}
\]
We next lower-bound the posterior uncertainty in this arm.

Let \(P_+^{(m)}\) and \(P_-^{(m)}\) denote the laws of its \(m\) revealed signs conditional on \(B_{a_*}=1\) and \(B_{a_*}=-1\), respectively.  For one sign, direct summation gives Hellinger affinity \(\sqrt{1-\delta^2}\); independence conditional on \(B_{a_*}\) therefore gives
\[
\rho_m=\sum_x\sqrt{P_+^{(m)}(x)P_-^{(m)}(x)}
=(1-\delta^2)^{m/2}. \tag{7}
\]
Writing \(p_+\) and \(p_-\) for the two mass functions, Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{TV}(P_+^{(m)},P_-^{(m)})
&=\frac12\sum_x|\sqrt{p_+(x)}-\sqrt{p_-(x)}|
                    (\sqrt{p_+(x)}+\sqrt{p_-(x)})\\
&\le \sqrt{1-\rho_m^2}
=\sqrt{1-(1-\delta^2)^m}
\le \sqrt{m\delta^2}
\le\frac12. \tag{8}
\end{aligned}
\]
The penultimate inequality follows by expanding \(1-(1-x)^m\le mx\) for \(x\in[0,1]\), and the last follows from (3) and (6).

Let \(q(x)=\mathbb E[B_{a_*}\mid x]\) under the equal mixture of \(P_+^{(m)}\) and \(P_-^{(m)}\).  Bayes' rule gives
\[
q(x)=\frac{p_+(x)-p_-(x)}{p_+(x)+p_-(x)}
\]
whenever the denominator is positive.  Integrating against the mixture mass \((p_++p_-)/2\) gives
\[
\mathbb E|q|=\operatorname{TV}(P_+^{(m)},P_-^{(m)}). \tag{9}
\]
Since \(|q|\le1\), equations (8)--(9) imply
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\operatorname{Var}(B_{a_*}\mid x)\right]
=1-\mathbb E[q(x)^2]
\ge1-\mathbb E|q(x)|
\ge\frac12. \tag{10}
\]

Given \(B_{a_*}\), the \(L\) unobserved endpoint signs in this arm remain conditionally independent, each with mean \(\delta B_{a_*}\) and variance \(1-\delta^2\).  Applying the conditional variance identity first given the revealed signs and then given \(B_{a_*}\), and using (10), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\mathbb E\!\left[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(
\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}\xi_{i,a_*}\,\middle|\,
z,\text{ observed outcomes}
\right)\,\middle|\,z\right]\\
&\quad=\frac1{n^2}\mathbb E\!\left[
L(1-\delta^2)+L^2\delta^2
\operatorname{Var}(B_{a_*}\mid x)\,\middle|\,z\right]\\
&\quad\ge\frac{L^2\delta^2}{2n^2}. \tag{11}
\end{aligned}
\]
By (1), (2), and (6), \(L=n-m\ge n-b(G)\ge n/2\).  Substitution of (3) into (11) therefore yields
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(
\frac1n\sum_i\xi_{i,a_*}\,\middle|\,
z,\text{ observed outcomes}
\right)\,\middle|\,z\right]
\ge \frac1{32B}. \tag{12}
\]

The two arm priors are independent, and conditional on \(z\) their likelihood factors by arm.  Consequently the posterior covariance between the two endpoint means is zero.  Since
\[
\tau_G(y)=\frac1n\sum_i(\xi_{i1}-\xi_{i0}), \tag{13}
\]
the posterior variance of \(\tau_G(y)\) is the sum of the two arm posterior variances; its expectation conditional on \(z\) is therefore at least the lower bound in (12).

Let \(\mathcal F\) contain \(G\), \(Z\), \(y(Z)\), and any estimator random seed.  Outcome independence of the design and independence of the estimator seed from the prior ensure that neither carries additional information about the endpoint signs beyond the observations just analyzed.  For every \(\mathcal F\)-measurable estimator \(T_*\), completing the square conditionally gives
\[
\mathbb E[(T_*-\tau_G)^2]
=\mathbb E[(T_*-\mathbb E[\tau_G\mid\mathcal F])^2]
+\mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(\tau_G\mid\mathcal F)]
\ge\frac1{32B}. \tag{14}
\]
The Bayes risk in (14) is no larger than the supremum risk over the support of the prior, which is contained in \(\mathcal M_2(G)\) by (5).  Since the same prior was used for every admissible design--estimator pair, taking the infimum specified by \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\) proves
\[
R_2(G)\ge\frac1{32B}
=\frac1{32\max\{1,b(G)\}}. \tag{15}
\]
Finally, (2) turns (15) into \(R_2(G)\ge1/(16n)\).

For the required smallest-instance audit, take \(n=4\) and \(d=0\).  Then \(E_1(z)=\{i:z_i=1\}\) and \(E_0(z)=\{i:z_i=0\}\), so enumeration by the treated count gives \(b(G)=2\).  Formula (15) gives \(R_2(G)\ge1/64\).  At the opposite finite boundary \(G=K_4\), every nonconstant assignment has \(E_1(z)=E_0(z)=\varnothing\), while a constant assignment exposes only one arm; hence \(b(G)=0\) and (15) gives \(R_2(G)\ge1/32\).  Both checks agree with (1)--(15), including the \(\max\{1,b(G)\}\) convention at \(b(G)=0\).

added_lemmas.gap: The lemma does not assert a random-regular upper bound on \(b(G)\); that is the missing combinatorial step behind the discarded logarithmic-scale lower edge.
added_lemmas.consumer: The repaired lower theorem uses its universal \(\Omega(n^{-1})\) branch, and the repaired bracket uses it at the bounded-degree elbow.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the global average treatment effect under arbitrary neighborhood interference and separate empirical second-moment bounds on its two endpoint arms, if \(G_n\) is uniformly random among simple labeled \(d\)-regular graphs and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), then there is a universal constant \(c_0>0\) such that
\[
\Pr_{G_n}\!\left\{R_2(G)\ge c_0\frac d n\right\}\longrightarrow1.
\]

The stronger lower edge of order \(r(n,d)\) is not asserted.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an index \(n\) and suppose \(d=0\).  Because \(G\) is a simple \(0\)-regular graph, it has no edges.  Hence \(N_G[i]=\{i\}\), \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)=\infty\) for distinct \(i,j\in V\), and
\[
F_G(A)=V\setminus A. \tag{1}
\]
In particular, \(|F_G(A)|=n-k\ge k\), since \(k\le\lfloor n/4\rfloor\).  Thus the first capsule trial is accepted under \(\text{def:reservoir-capsule}\).

Conditional on \(A\), the set \(C\) is uniform among the \(k\)-subsets of \(V\setminus A\).  Moreover, for each fixed \(k\)-subset \(S\subseteq V\),
\[
\Pr(C=S\mid G)
=\sum_{\substack{A\subseteq V:\ |A|=k,\ A\cap S=\varnothing}}
 \frac{1}{\binom nk}\frac{1}{\binom{n-k}{k}}
=\frac{\binom{n-k}{k}}{\binom nk\binom{n-k}{k}}
=\frac1{\binom nk}. \tag{2}
\]
Thus both \(A\) and \(C\) are marginally uniform \(k\)-subsets, and they are disjoint.  The independent fair arm-swap coin therefore makes each of \(T\) and \(C_0\) marginally uniform among the \(k\)-subsets of \(V\), while \(T\cap C_0=\varnothing\).  By \(\text{def:reservoir-capsule}\), the units outside \(T\cup C_0\) receive conditionally independent fair assignments.  This proves the asserted description of the design.

For each \(i\in V\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\), (2) and the arm swap give
\[
\pi_{(i,a)}=\frac{k}{n}>0. \tag{3}
\]
Since the accepted capsule reveals the appropriate endpoint by \(\text{prop:capsule-realization}\), substitution of (3) into \(\text{def:raw-estimator}\) yields the well-defined raw estimator
\[
\widetilde\tau_G
=\frac1k\sum_{i\in T}y_{i1}-\frac1k\sum_{i\in C_0}y_{i0}. \tag{4}
\]
Each term in (4) is a simple-random-sample mean of its fixed endpoint array.  Indeed, if \(S\) is a uniform \(k\)-subset, \(I_i=\mathbf 1\{i\in S\}\), \(\bar x=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i\), and \(\bar x_S=k^{-1}\sum_i I_i x_i\), then
\[
\mathbb E I_i=\frac{k}{n},\qquad
\mathbb E(I_iI_j)=\frac{k(k-1)}{n(n-1)}\quad(i\ne j). \tag{5}
\]
Expanding the variance with (5) gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\bar x_S)
=\frac{n-k}{k(n-1)}\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}(x_i-\bar x)^2\right\}. \tag{6}
\]
In particular, (5) also shows directly that the two sample means in (4) are unbiased for the corresponding population endpoint means, so (4) is unbiased for \(\tau_G\).

For every \(y\in\mathcal M_2(G)\), the two endpoint moment restrictions in \(\text{def:endpoint-class}\) imply
\[
\frac1n\sum_i(y_{ia}-\bar y_a)^2
=\frac1n\sum_i y_{ia}^2-\bar y_a^2\le 1,
\qquad a\in\{0,1\}. \tag{7}
\]
Writing the two sample means in (4) as \(U\) and \(W\), respectively, the elementary inequality
\(\operatorname{Var}(U-W)\le 2\operatorname{Var}(U)+2\operatorname{Var}(W)\), together with (6)--(7), gives
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}
\mathbb E[(\widetilde\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]
\le \frac{4(n-k)}{k(n-1)}. \tag{8}
\]
Condition (3) permits application of \(\text{lem:exact-risk-certificate}\), which proves that \(\widehat\tau_G\) is unbiased and that Rao--Blackwellization cannot increase the mean squared error.  Consequently the left side of (8) remains an upper bound with \(\widehat\tau_G\) in place of \(\widetilde\tau_G\).  Finally,
\[
\frac{k}{n}\longrightarrow \frac{\log 2}{32}, \tag{9}
\]
because \(0<\log 2/32<1/4\).  Equations (8)--(9) show that the capsule and its Rao--Blackwell estimator constitute an admissible outcome-independent design--estimator pair with worst-case risk \(O(n^{-1})\).  By \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\),
\[
R_2(G)\le \frac{C}{n} \tag{10}
\]
for an absolute constant \(C\) and all sufficiently large \(n\).

It remains to show that no other outcome-independent design and estimator can improve the order in (10).  Introduce a prior consisting of mutually independent Rademacher variables \(\{\varepsilon_{ia}:i\in V,\ a\in\{0,1\}\}\), and, for every prior realization, define the entire potential-outcome schedule by
\[
y_i(z)=\varepsilon_{i,z_i}. \tag{11}
\]
Because \(N_G[i]=\{i\}\), equality of \(z\) and \(z'\) on \(N_G[i]\) implies \(z_i=z_i'\), so (11) satisfies \(\text{ass:ani}\).  Its endpoints obey
\[
\frac1n\sum_i y_{ia}^2=1,
\qquad a\in\{0,1\}, \tag{12}
\]
so every schedule in the support of this prior belongs to \(\mathcal M_2(G)\) by \(\text{def:endpoint-class}\).

Now fix any outcome-independent assignment law \(\mathsf D\).  Independence of the design from the schedule implies that, conditional on a realized assignment \(Z=z\) and observed outcomes \(y(z)=(\varepsilon_{i,z_i})_{i\in V}\), the unobserved variables \(\varepsilon_{i,1-z_i}\) remain mutually independent Rademacher variables.  The target decomposes as
\[
\tau_G
=\frac1n\sum_{i\in V}
\left\{(2z_i-1)\varepsilon_{i,z_i}
 +(1-2z_i)\varepsilon_{i,1-z_i}\right\}. \tag{13}
\]
The first summand inside the braces is observed, whereas each term in the second summand has conditional variance one and the terms are conditionally independent.  Therefore, for the observed-data sigma-field \(\mathscr O=\sigma(G,Z,y(Z))\),
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\tau_G\mid\mathscr O)
=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i\in V}(1-2Z_i)^2
=\frac1n \quad\text{almost surely}. \tag{14}
\]
For any possibly randomized estimator \(T_*\) based on \(\mathscr O\), adjoin its independent randomization seed to \(\mathscr O\).  Conditional expectation is the squared-error minimizer, and the seed contains no information about the unobserved endpoint signs; hence
\[
\mathbb E[(T_*-\tau_G)^2]
\ge \mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(\tau_G\mid\mathscr O)]
=\frac1n. \tag{15}
\]
The prior is supported on \(\mathcal M_2(G)\) by (11)--(12), so the supremum risk of this fixed pair \((\mathsf D,T_*)\) is at least its prior-average risk in (15).  Taking the infimum over all eligible pairs in \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\) gives
\[
R_2(G)\ge \frac1n. \tag{16}
\]
Combining (10) and (16) proves \(R_2(G)=\Theta(n^{-1})\) when \(d=0\).

For the required smallest-instance audit, take \(n=4\).  Then \(k=1\).  There are twelve ordered choices \((T,C_0)\) with distinct entries, each equally likely, and the two remaining units have four equiprobable fair-coin assignments conditional on that pair.  On every such design history (4) equals \(y_{T,1}-y_{C_0,0}\), and direct averaging over the twelve ordered pairs gives
\[
\frac1{12}\sum_{t\ne c}(y_{t1}-y_{c0})
=\frac14\sum_{i=1}^4(y_{i1}-y_{i0})
=\tau_G. \tag{17}
\]
The treated count is \(1+\operatorname{Binomial}(2,1/2)\), so it takes the values \(1,2,3\); thus the audit also confirms that the capsule is the stated two-stage design rather than a fixed balanced complete randomization.  Under the supported prior (11), (14) equals \(1/4\) for every assignment in this enumeration, confirming the lower-bound calculation at the boundary instance.
